exclusions.query: Hausdorff dimension bound of the singular set below the varifold dimension
exclusions.reason: The statement only gives measure zero in the dimension of the varifold.

prerequisites.concept: almost-everywhere regularity of stationary integral varifolds

outputs.exact_statement: Every stationary integral $m$-varifold in an open subset of $\mathbb R^{m+n}$ satisfies $$\mathcal H^m(\operatorname{Sing}V)=0.$$ Here $m,n\geq1$ are arbitrary. No stability, minimizing, orientability, density upper bound, or codimension-one hypothesis is required.

Let $m,n\geq1$ and let $V$ be an integral $m$-varifold on the full unit round sphere $S^{m+n}$, stationary for variations tangent to the sphere. A support point is regular if on a spherical neighborhood $V=q|\Sigma|$ for an integer $q\geq1$ and a smooth embedded minimal $m$-submanifold $\Sigma$ of the sphere. If $\operatorname{Sing}_S V$ denotes the remaining support points, then $$\mathcal H^m_{g_{\mathrm{round}}}(\operatorname{Sing}_S V)=0.$$ No fixed upper bound on mass, density, or multiplicity is required, nor are stability, orientability, or mod-two cyclicity. The same conclusion holds on every round sphere of positive radius.

Set $u=(y-x)/s$, $A(s)=s^2M_s(x)$, and $$R_s(x)=\int G_s(y-x)B[u,u]\,\mathop{}\!d\mu.$$ In flat coordinates, apart from $\mathcal T_s$, $$\label{eq:lt-gaussian-flat}
 \dot A=s^2L_s+s^2R_s,
 \qquad \dot{}=\frac{\mathop{}\!d}{\mathop{}\!d\log s}.$$ In the curved coordinates fixed above, $$\label{eq:lt-gaussian-curved}
 \dot A=s^2L_s+s^2R_s+\mathcal E_s+\mathcal T_s,
 \qquad
 |\mathcal E_s|\le C\gamma s^2
           \int G_s(y-x)(1+|u|^2)\,\mathop{}\!d\tau(y).$$ Here the entries of $u$ in $B[u,u]$ are taken in the chosen orthonormal horizontal frame, and $\gamma$ retains its definition from the fixed physical coordinates.

Let $f$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $X$, with $M_f=f(X)>0$, and let $K$ be the entrance boundary of a continuation set. There is a probability measure $\sigma$ on $K$ such that the positive spatial measure $$h=M_f(\pi_X)_\#\sigma$$ has mass $M_f$ and, at every $(x,s_0)\in\mathop{\mathrm{spt}}\sigma$, $$\label{ct:contact-signs}
 (f-h)_{s_0}(x)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \int_{s_0}^{s}v^2(f-h)_v(x)\,\mathop{}\!d\log v\ge0
 \quad(s\ge s_0).$$ The second inequality concerns the integral; it does not assert a pointwise sign at scales larger than $s_0$.

The mass $\widehat h_\sigma(K_\sigma\setminus\mathcal G_\sigma)$ is at most $$o_{\sigma\downarrow0}(1)+Cd_*d.$$ Every contact in $\mathcal G_\sigma$ has a scale $s_0\in[\underline s,\rho)$ with $\tau_{s_0}(x)=d_*$. The inequalities [ex:threshold-control] hold also when $\underline s

Set $$I(s)=\max\left\{
   \sup_{s\le v\le\rho}(s/v)^K A(v),\,
   (s/\rho)^K\rho^2d\rho^{-2m-4}\right\},
 \qquad a(s)=\log\frac{s^2}{I(s)}.
 \label{ex:future}$$ Starting at a threshold scale $s_0$, stop at the first scale $s_*$ with $a(s_*)=T/2$. This scale exists, and on the path $[s_0,s_*]$ one has $$a(s_0)=a_0+O(1),\qquad a(s)\ge a_0-O(1),\qquad
 v^2\tau_v\le C(v/s)^K I(s)\quad(s\le v\le\rho).
 \label{ex:dilations}$$ The functions $I,a$ are locally Lipschitz in $\log s$. Almost everywhere they satisfy $$\begin{cases}
 I=A,\quad \dot I=\dot A,&\text{on the reset set }\{I=A\},\\
 \dot I=KI,&\text{on its complement},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 |\dot a|+\dfrac{|\dot I|+|\dot Z|}{I}\le C.
 \label{ex:derivatives}$$ Moreover $\dot Z/I$ is locally Lipschitz, with derivative bounded by $C$. For every fixed $P$, weighted scalar control gives $$|M|_s\le C(D_s+\Lambda_s)+a^{-P}I(s)/s^2.
 \label{ex:weighted-scalar}$$ All constants are uniform in the contact and the bottom.

At $s_0$ one can choose at most $Q$ wells and a small parameter $k_0>0$ so that the barrier of [ex:barrier](#ex:barrier) holds initially. If more than one well is used, one may arrange, for any fixed $P$, $$Z(s_0)\le a_0^{-P}I(s_0),\qquad U(s_0)\le CI(s_0),$$ before any immediate mergers, with $k_0$ a small fixed constant. Alternatively there is one common well, with $$U(s_0)\le CS_h(a_0)^2 I(s_0),\qquad
 I(s_0)-Z(s_0)\ge cS_h(a_0)^{-2}I(s_0),
 \qquad k_0=cS_h(a_0)^{-6}.$$ For $Q=1$, $k_0$ is a small fixed constant.

Fix $\varepsilon_0>0$, sufficiently small for the later packing argument, and any fixed loss exponent $C_*$. For large $T$, there are $Q$ ordered disjoint bands $[B_i,2B_i]\subset(2a_0,T/2)$, independent of the contact, such that $$B_1^{1/10}\gg F_Q(T)^3,\qquad S_h(a_0)^{C_*}\ll B_1^{\varepsilon_0},\qquad S_1(2B_i)^{C_*}\ll B_{i+1}^{\varepsilon_0}. \label{ex:band-spacing}$$ For $Q=1$, only the first condition is needed, and a single band of size comparable to $T$ suffices. Every contact path has a traversal contained in one band, from $a=B$ to $a=2B$, which contains no merger and on which $k\ge B^{-\varepsilon_0}$. The estimates [ex:bank], [ex:dilations], [ex:derivatives], [ex:weighted-scalar], and [ex:comparison]–[ex:transition] hold on that traversal. If it has several wells, the bound $\dot Z\le a^{-P_0}I$ holds on every preceding stage with several wells as well, and the initial value of $Z$ is the arbitrarily small quantity in [ex:initialization](#ex:initialization).

Fix $0<c_0<1/10$ and a tilt threshold $\varepsilon_0>0$. By reducing the admissible upper bound for $m_0$ in [ce:fit](#ce:fit), there is a constant $c>0$ with the following property. If the first failure at $x$ has scale $\ell$, then in every base ball of radius $c_0\ell$ whose center lies in $B_{30\ell}(x)$, normal projection onto the failed fit has a subset of base volume at least $c\ell^m$ on which the total integer count is $Q$ and two entries have separation at least $c m_0\ell^{k_0}$. Those two entries have tilt at most $\varepsilon_0$ relative to the fit and each has multiplicity strictly less than $Q$. The word “entry” refers to a point where the projection Jacobian is nonzero, with its integer multiplicity; no smoothness of a sheet is asserted. In particular no failure occurs when $Q=1$.

Fix the desired output order $J\ge6$, apply [ce:fit](#ce:fit) with derivative order $J+1$, and then choose its corresponding $k_0$ and initial parameters. There is a $C^J$ graph $S$ on an interior neighborhood of $0$, with $C^J$ norm at most $Cm_0$, through $0$ and tangent to $P_0$ there, and a nonnegative Lipschitz function $t$ on the fixed base, such that $$\label{ce:geometry}
 |H_S|+|\nabla H_S|\le Cm_0^2t^{2k_0-4},
 \qquad
 |z|\le Cm_0t^{k_0}\quad\hbox{on }\mathop{\mathrm{spt}}\mu.$$ In the first inequality $t$ is evaluated at the horizontal coordinate of the point of $S$; in the second it may be evaluated either at $\pi_0X$ or at $\pi_0\pi_SX$, with a change of constant. Writing $\mathcal I=\{t>0\}$, one has $$\label{ce:influence}
 t(0)=0,\qquad
 \sup_{B_r}t=o(r),\qquad
 |\mathcal I\cap B_r|=o(r^m).$$ In particular the support height is zero off the influence region. On $S$ itself its normal-projection version has the same vanishing volume density. If $\rho$ is distance to $0$ on $S$, then $|z|\le C\rho^2$ on the support in a sufficiently small tube.
If the support lies on the center $S$ in a neighborhood of the origin, then the origin is regular.

On all sufficiently small radii, $P$ is bounded above and below. For each fixed $\lambda\in(0,1)$ there are constants $C_\lambda,c_\lambda>0$ such that $$\label{in:doubling}
 c_\lambda H(r)\leq H(\lambda r)\leq C_\lambda H(r),
 \qquad
 \int_{\lambda r}^{r}q_*(v)\,\frac{\mathop{}\!dv}{v}\leq C_\lambda.$$ There is a sequence $r_j\downarrow0$ on which both $n_*(r_j)$ and $q_*(r_j)$ are bounded.
The positive-height alternative at the origin is impossible. Consequently every point satisfying the typical-point hypotheses [ce:typical] is regular.
